messages:
incident-bot: PAGE -> on-call: detected SLO breach on /v1/generate (streaming). p95 0.47s, p99 1.86s (>1.5s SLO). tail spikes correlated with 'prompt_preproc' service. auto-escalate to #incidents and paging rotation.

mike: acked, taking lead. I'm oncall, will triage now. any customer-facing alerts?

aisha: looking at traces — most p99s are in preproc/tokenizer stage, not model. We have a cluster of long-running preproc jobs hitting CPU and parsing-heavy paths. Affected endpoints: streaming + json-mode (tool-schema heavy).

sam: logs show huge prompt templates and nested tool schemas triggering a regex/serde hotspot. snippet from preproc logs:
```
[2026-03-15T12:07:11Z] req_id=abc123 stage=template_hydration size=37842 bytes parse_time=512ms regex_compile=210ms json_unmarshal=180ms
[2026-03-15T12:07:11Z] req_id=def456 stage=tokenize kvprefix=... tokenize_time=680ms
```
this matches the tail we see in traces.

ravi: chiming in — tokenizer itself is fine for normal prompts, but when prompt templates include massive tool schemas + JSON-mode formatting we hit two things: (1) large string allocations & repeated regexes during hydration, (2) JSON-mode runs additional validation steps per request. Combined with continuous-batching timing we get streaming stalls.

aisha: immediate mitigation options I propose:
1) scale preproc workers +2 (provisioned) to relieve CPU pressure
2) flip json-mode off for streaming route for the next 30 minutes for all customers — will reduce validation cost
3) enable prompt-template cache for top N templates (fast path)
4) add temporary rate-limit on prompt size > 32k bytes (429 for now)
which one do folks want first?

julia: CS says 3 small customers are seeing errors/timeouts (IDs: C-9821, C-5552, C-1010). We should message them if we toggle behavior. Prefer config change that avoids 429s first.

mike: agree. Sam, can you push a quick config to flip json-mode off for streaming routes (canary to region-us then global) + add autoscale? I'll hand off after that.

sam: working on a canary now. applying route override:
```bash
redwoodctl routes update --route /v1/generate --override '{"streaming": {"json_mode": false}}' --region us-east-1 --canary 10
redwoodctl autoscale set --service preproc --min 4 --max 12 --scale-in-delay 90s
```
I'll watch metrics.

deploy-bot: Deploy started by sam. Change: route override (streaming json_mode=false) canary=10% region=us-east-1.

aisha: metric check — after canary went live at 12:12 UTC we saw immediate drop in p99 in us-east-1 from 1.9s -> 1.1s for streaming requests hitting the canary. CPU on preproc pods in canary pool dropped from 92% -> 48%.

nora: support pinged the impacted customers, told them we are applying mitigations and might change formatting behavior for streaming while we investigate. customers want a quick postmortem.

sam: rolling to 100% now. also pushed prompt-template-cache for top 50 hashed templates.

deploy-bot: Rollout status: canary OK -> 100% applied. prompt cache enabled on preproc. autoscale updated.

mike: handing off to sam for monitoring and follow-up. I'm going to sleep but will check in if SLOs bounce.

aisha: LIVE UPDATE: 12:30 UTC global p99 back to 0.95s, p95 0.42s. streaming tail stalls reduced. Marking incident as mitigated for now.

ravi: temporary root cause summary: prompt-hydration + JSON-mode validation for large tool schemas created a CPU/regex hotspot in preproc. Streaming semantics amplified tail due to batching/timers.

julia: action items for follow-up (post-incident):
- engineering: add compile-once regex cache and avoid repeated regex_compile on each request (owner: eng-preproc)
- engineering: add preflight prompt-size rejection and better error (owner: eng-runtime)
- product/CS: better docs + warn customers about heavy tool-schema costs in JSON-mode (owner: product-docs)
- infra: refine autoscale policy for preproc to react to parse_latency/p99 (owner: eng-sre)
- security/infra: review any customer data change due to temporary json-mode disable (owner: compliance)

aisha: creating a follow-up ticket now: INC-3199 with logs, traces, and customer list. I'll attach a REPRO that simulates a 40k-byte template to benchmark fixes.

mike: thanks team. No longer paging. If anything flares, @sam please re-escalate. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident mitigated — SLOs restored. Next steps documented in INC-3199.
